Change c0342. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. I; 1831 Ch. XVIII.

Context before (unchanged): I revolved rapidly in my mind a multitude of thoughts, and endeavoured to arrive at some conclusion.

1818 text: Alas! to me the idea of an immediate union with my cousin was one of horror and dismay.

1831 text: Alas! to me the idea of an immediate union with my Elizabeth was one of horror and dismay.

Diff: Alas! to me the idea of an immediate union with my [-cousin-] {+Elizabeth+} was one of horror and dismay.

Context after (unchanged): I was bound by a solemn promise, which I had not yet fulfilled, and dared not break; or, if I did, what manifold miseries might not impend over me and my devoted family!

result.rationale: Replaces the kinship term "cousin" with the personal name "Elizabeth", so the narrator now presents her as an individual loved figure rather than a relation, which shifts how the marriage horror reads.
